business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European; unitary national codification under the Código Civil and Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-China BIT (1992, as amended by the 2005 Protocol)
Spain-United States DTA (1990, with 2013 Amending Protocol)
International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage (Bunkers Convention 2001, in force for Spain since 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 4, 14, 32-34), as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Loi 10/2010); Real Decreto-ley 6/2023 and Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio (creation of the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales - RCTR); Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, arts. 21-23); Circular del Banco de España 8/2016; SEPBLAC interpretative guidance for medium-risk commercial sectors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (Name Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Ministry of Justice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic administrative certificate; no apostille required for the Spanish incorporation procedure

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each director, shareholder, and final beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the holder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille + notarized copy + sworn translation into Spanish if issued in a non-Spanish/EU language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / company register extract of each corporate shareholder (if any corporate UBO is involved)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry of the jurisdiction of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states) + sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and evidence of funds evidencing the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding credit institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the issuing bank + Hague Apostille + sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form for the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (RCTR) and PEP questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary / external AML legal counsel in Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed in the presence of a Spanish notary; filed electronically with the RCTR post-incorporation; government-only access per art. 34 Ley 10/2010

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification of PEPs and their family members/closely associated persons per art. 14 Ley 10/2010 with enhanced due diligence for PEPs from high-risk third jurisdictions. Screening required against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (CFSP implementing regulations), SEPBLAC alerts, and Banco de España risk classifications. OFAC SDN screening is contractually imposed by Spanish banks as a condition for USD SWIFT Wire and Standby LC payment rails. All directors, shareholders, UBOs, commercial counterparties, and vessel counterparties must be screened at onboarding, before each bunkering transaction, and at least annually thereafter due to the medium-risk AML tier assigned to ISIC 5222.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.sl_minimum_capital_note: Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) permits incorporation of an SL with a minimum capital of EUR 1, subject to the obligation to constitute a legal reserve until capital plus reserves reach EUR 3,000. For bunkering licensing and P&I insurance purposes a promoter contribution of at least EUR 3,500 is recommended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Colegio de Registradores de España (Registro Mercantil Central - RMC) via https://www.registradores.org and CIRCE portal (https://portal.circe.es) for electronic SL incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in Castilian Spanish (basic Latin script with Ñ). The RMC applies phonetic equivalence examination; transliterations such as K/C, W/U, Y/I and any hybrid scripts may cause non-vetting or rejection. The name must contain or be accompanied by the legal form 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' (the normalized short form 'SL' is accepted in the RMC index). Names in co-official Spanish languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician) are admissible within their linguistic regime but must still use Latin script and comply with RMC phonetic rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name clearance certificate from the RMC is valid for 90 days and no formal extension exists; if the company deed is not executed within this window, a new application (with up to five alternative names) must be filed. Upon rejection, the RMC issues a formal denial. The applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, attaching the denial certificate, legal argument, and, if applicable, prior trademark evidence. The DGSJFP must resolve within three months. Given the 90-day certificate deadlock, parallel alternative name applications and execution of the deed with the first available name are strongly recommended to avoid blocking incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office address is NOT acceptable as the sole statutory registered office for an SL conducting regulated bunkering supply (ISIC 5222). The Commercial Registry and the competent Port Authority require a physical, accessible office in Spanish territory where corporate books, UBO documentation, insurance certificates and operating permits are kept. A virtual address may be used only as a supplementary commercial correspondence address after the physical registered office is proven.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the competent Autoridad Portuaria and/or a SEPBLAC on-site compliance review within the first 18 months of bunkering operations, due to the medium-risk AML classification and port-environment controls.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.license_prerequisite_note: Prior to commercial commencement, the SL must obtain the relevant bunkering supply authorization from the competent Autoridad Portuaria (e.g., Algeciras, Valencia, Barcelona, Bilbao) under Real Decreto Legislativo 2/2011 (Ley de Puertos del Estado y de la Marina Mercante) and Ley 14/2014 (Ley de Navegación Marítima), plus enrollment in the national registry of fuel suppliers to vessels if applicable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance application to the Registro Mercantil Central (up to 5 name choices)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Spanish Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff regulated by the Spanish Ministry of Justice (BOE fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the articles of association (Estatutos Sociales) and incorporation minutes by Spanish corporate counsel
Notarial public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución de SL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notarial College (Colegio Notarial del territorio where the deed is executed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (Arancel Notarial, Real Decreto 1426/1989)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traductor-jurado) and apostille/consular legalization of foreign shareholder and UBO identity and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor-Jurado (Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff of the traductor-jurado plus apostille processing fee (Hague Convention, is generally free at Spanish authorities; overseas fees vary)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) including publication in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of the competent Provincial Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff (Real Decreto 1784/1996 carrying charges) plus BORME publication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification questionnaire, AML risk assessment, PEP and sanctions screening file (Stage 1 due diligence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed professional fee for medium-risk enhanced onboarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary licensing consultation and feasibility check with the competent Port Authority (Autoridad Portuaria) for bunkering supply
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Autoridad Portuaria (administrative consultation) and/or marine consultancy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative consultation fee plus external consultancy rate (market benchmark)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): arts. 19-24 (constitución), arts. 4 and 62 (minimum capital and full payment), arts. 22-39 (estatutos), arts. 209-230 (administration); Real Decreto 1784/1996, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RRM); Ley 14/2013 (apoyo a los emprendedores) enabling telematic incorporation via CIRCE; RDL 2/2011 for port service licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the provincial capital where the registered office is located; public deed executed before a Notario of the Colegio Notarial de España.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public incorporation deed), submitted for mandatory inscription (primera inscripción) in the Registro Mercantil; official tariffs comprise notarial arancel, registry arancel and name-certificate fee, variable by capital and region.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum capital, fully subscribed and paid in cash before execution of the deed (LSC arts. 4 and 62); capital is deposited in a Spanish credit institution in the name of the company in formation and attested by a bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) annexed to the deed; no statutory escrow account is required. Sociedad de Formación Sucesiva exceptions apply only below EUR 3,000 with statutory reserve restrictions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporation deed of the Company, executed before a Spanish notary, is ratified, and the subscription and full payment of the EUR 3,000 share capital, evidenced by the bank deposit certificate, is approved. (2) The registered office is fixed at [registered-office address], Spain, with corporate objects covering wholesale marine fuel, lubricant and bunkering supply to vessels under ISIC 5222. (3) Mr./Ms. [full name] is appointed Sole Administrator for an indefinite term with power to open bank accounts, procure the definitive NIF, and file all port, environmental and operating license applications. (4) The Sole Administrator may delegate execution of ancillary documents and engage advisors. Adopted unanimously by the founding members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Company Name Certificate (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid, via CIRCE telematic portal or through the notary channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File one signed application requesting up to three corporate name alternatives; the Central Registry checks for identical or confusingly similar names and issues the certificate in approximately 3 working days; the certificate is valid for 3 months and must be delivered to the notary at deed execution.
required_dossiers: Signed name reservation application form (solicitud de certificación de denominación)
Passport or NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) of each founding member
Tax residency certificate or UBO declaration for non-resident members
Notarized power of attorney and official Spanish translation if filed by a representative
Registry fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns a coinciding-name refusal, submit a revised application with up to three new names; an administrative appeal lies to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months, but the faster cure is alternative-name resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Deposit Account and Pay In Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution regulated by Banco de España, selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name 'ES_SL en constitución'; each founder transfers the subscribed cash quota until the aggregate equals at least EUR 3,000; the bank issues a certificado de depósito bancario identifying the depositors and amounts for annexure to the deed. Given the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML tier for marine fuel bunkering (Ley 10/2010), enhanced due diligence applies; accounts should support SWIFT wire and standby LC operations for the planned payment rails.
required_dossiers: Account opening application executed by the authorized signatories
Passport/NIE and UBO declaration (titularidad real) of each signatory and effective controller
Copy of the negative name certificate or draft deed of incorporation
Source-of-funds documentation for all contributed amounts
Charter and corporate identification of each corporate shareholder (Apostilled and translated)
AML/KYC questionnaire completed for the marine fuel trading activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account for AML review, supply clarified source-of-funds evidence and audited financial statements of the contributing shareholders; alternatively, deposit the capital before a notary and attach the notarial deposit receipt to the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Incorporation Deed before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario authorized by the Colegio Notarial de España in the province of the statutory registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment with all founders or their notarial attorneys presenting the name certificate, bank deposit certificate and approved draft bylaws; the notary verifies legal capacity, capital payment, and legality of the corporate object, then executes the deed and issues an authorized first copy for registry inscription; the notary also files the incorporation electronically with AEAT and the Registro Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate valid within 3 months
Bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso)
Draft bylaws (estatutos sociales) compliant with LSC arts. 22-39
NIE certificate and passport of each founding member or notarial power of attorney
UBO declaration per Ley 10/2010
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to statutory defects, amend the bylaws to comply with the LSC and reschedule; a negative opinion may be reviewed by the Colegio Notarial or cured by engaging another notary in the same province.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Consejería de Hacienda / Servicio Tributario of the Autonomous Community of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days after deed execution, self-assess Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados in the Actos Jurídicos Documentados modality on the paid-in capital, at the regional rate normally between 0.5% and 1.5%; file Modelo 600 online and pay electronically; the stamped receipt accompanies the registry application.
required_dossiers: Modelo 600 self-assessment declaration
Authorized first copy of the notarial deed with party NIFs
Bank payment acknowledgement of the assessed tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional tax office reassesses the base or denies an exemption, file a Modelo 600 rectification within the voluntary period or pay the assessed difference with recargo and late-interest; appeals follow Ley General Tributaria arts. 120 and 222.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is situated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original authorized first copy of the deed, the Modelo 600 paid receipt, and the signed instancia de inscripción; the Registrador Mercantil qualifies the deed within 15 legal days, normally 7-10 working days; upon inscription the registry issues the certification of incorporation required for the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Original first copy of the incorporation deed
Modelo 600 stamped receipt from the regional tax office
Instancia de inscripción signed by the appointed administrator
NIE of the administrator and written acceptance of office
Bylaws text for the registry file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a nota de calificación desfavorable, cure each defect and re-present within the suspension period, or appeal the qualification before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive Tax ID (NIF) and Complete Censal Registration with AEAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), provincial office with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry inscription, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF, declare commencement of activity under ISIC 5222/NAICS 488390, and elect VAT and Corporate Income Tax obligations; the notary's electronic filing accelerates issuance; non-resident administrators must appoint a Spanish tax representative where required.
required_dossiers: Certificación literal of the Mercantile Registry inscription
Authorized first copy of the deed
Modelo 036/037 censal declaration of commencement of operations
NIF of the administrator and appointment resolution
Proof of registered office (lease contract or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT withholds the definitive NIF pending information, submit the registry certificate, the appointment resolution and shareholder identification; rectify omissions via Modelo 036 and, for non-residents, appoint a fiscal representative to cure the deficiency.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The competent tax administration is national, subject to specific regional tax arrangements not applicable to mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT after incorporation documentation is available and obtain the definitive NIF after registration details are completed. The application is generally made using Modelo 036, submitted electronically by an authorized representative or, where permitted, at an AEAT office. Required evidence normally includes the public deed of incorporation, Commercial Registry filing or registration evidence, articles of association, identification and powers of the legal representative, and identification of shareholders or beneficial owners when requested. Non-resident corporate shareholders generally require a Spanish NIF for tax identification and may need a representative or power of attorney for AEAT procedures. The Spanish NIF is also used as the VAT identification number, normally in the format ES plus the entity's NIF. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036 is required for qualifying intra-EU transactions and inclusion in VIES. A foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment may obtain a Spanish NIF through its appointed representative or authorized agent where a Spanish tax filing, VAT obligation, customs operation, or other statutory tax procedure requires it. Customs Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) registration is separately required for customs activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person and does not have a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Spanish tax-transparent treatment is limited to specific statutory structures and does not ordinarily apply to an SL. The entity may access statutory regimes where eligibility conditions are met, including the reduced regime for newly created entities, the regime for small entities, and qualifying special regimes such as the Canary Islands Zone regime, but these are not elective entity-classification elections. Spanish and EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, include income, or otherwise neutralize mismatches involving related parties or structured arrangements. Tax consolidation and other special regimes require formal elections and statutory conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), governed principally by Law 37/1992 and its implementing regulations. Customs operations are governed by the Union Customs Code and related EU legislation. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands apply Spanish VAT; the Canary Islands apply the separate IGIC regime, and Ceuta and Melilla are outside the Spanish VAT territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general Spanish VAT registration threshold applies. A person carrying out an economic activity must register from the commencement of taxable economic activity or before the relevant taxable operations occur, regardless of turnover. The NIF and census registration are generally completed through Modelo 036. Separate registration may be required for intra-EU transactions, distance sales, importation, customs activity, or special regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every VAT invoice. The Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, VAT groups, and entities that opt into the system, to electronically submit specified invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within statutory short filing periods. Royal Decree 1007/2023 establishes requirements for computerised invoicing and billing systems, including integrity, traceability, preservation, event logging, and, under the VERI*FACTU model, transmission of invoice records to the AEAT; implementation dates are subject to the applicable transitional rules and subsequent regulatory timetable. Business-to-business electronic invoicing under the Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies is being phased in through implementing regulations and is not equivalent to universal prior VAT clearance. Electronic invoices must satisfy Spanish and EU invoicing, authenticity, integrity, legibility, storage, and audit-access requirements. Customs electronic declarations and MRN-based export procedures apply to goods exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the supplier, purchaser, transport, and documentary evidence requirements are satisfied and the goods actually leave the VAT territory. Supplies to qualifying vessels used for navigation on the high seas and for specified commercial, industrial, or fishing activities, including qualifying fuel and provisions, may qualify for the specific vessel-related exemption under Article 22, subject to vessel status, use, delivery, and documentary conditions; bunker fuel is not automatically exempt merely because it is delivered to a ship. Intra-EU supplies require the applicable exemption conditions, including a valid customer VAT number, transport to another Member State, and correct EC Sales List reporting. Services are generally governed by place-of-supply rules rather than a blanket export zero rate. Bunkering, storage, delivery, and related logistics services must be analysed separately, including the special rules for services connected with immovable property, transport, vessels, and intermediary services where relevant. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, accounting records, proof of taxable business activity, and filing through the applicable domestic or non-established-business refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration accepted by Spanish Customs, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit or equivalent customs proof that the goods physically left the EU customs and VAT territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, quantity, value, VAT treatment, and relevant vessel or delivery details
Bill of lading, sea waybill, bunker delivery note, delivery receipt, or equivalent transport and receipt evidence identifying the vessel and delivered fuel or lubricants
Purchase order, contract, and evidence of the customer's entitlement to any vessel-related VAT exemption
Evidence of the vessel's registration, activity, and qualifying commercial, industrial, fishing, or navigation status where Article 22 exemption is claimed
Inventory, loading, meter, quantity, and custody records reconciling the invoiced products with the physically delivered products
Supplier accounting records, VAT return entries, and EC Sales List records where an intra-EU transaction is involved
Bank payment evidence and, where applicable, documentary evidence supporting the economic substance of the transaction and any VAT refund claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for VAT zero-rating or export exemption. The taxpayer must instead prove the taxable treatment and actual export or qualifying vessel supply within the statutory record-retention and assessment periods. If the exemption is unsupported or the goods did not leave the relevant territory, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties, and may deny or claw back related input VAT refunds. Under the General Tax Law, inaccurate or incomplete tax returns may generally attract penalties based on the unpaid or improperly refunded amount, commonly ranging from 50% to 150% depending on severity, concealment, fraud, repeated conduct, and the resulting tax loss; unjustified refunds and fraudulent documentation may trigger additional consequences. Customs infringements may lead to customs debt, recovery of duties and taxes, seizure or forfeiture measures, and administrative penalties under EU and Spanish customs law. Intentional tax fraud can constitute a criminal tax offence where the statutory thresholds and other Penal Code conditions are met, including the general tax-loss threshold of EUR 120,000 per tax and assessment period. Related-party, carousel-fraud, false-documentation, and fuel-diversion indicators receive heightened audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism; the Spanish Foreign Exchange Regulation is governed by Royal Decree 1816/1991 and subsequent amendments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible. Current account transactions (including trade in goods and services, dividends, and interest) are unrestricted. Capital account transactions (e.g., foreign direct investment, portfolio investment) are also liberalized, but require post-transaction statistical declaration to the Banco de España for amounts exceeding €1,000,000 or when the transaction involves tax havens. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to corporate income tax (25% standard rate) and potential withholding tax on dividends (19% for EU residents, 0% under certain EU directives). No exchange control approval is required for remittances, but banks must verify the underlying transaction and report to the authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds in Spain. Exporters may retain foreign currency in non-resident or resident foreign currency accounts. However, all export transactions must be declared to the Banco de España for statistical purposes within 30 days of the transaction if the amount exceeds EUR 12,500 (or equivalent). For bunkering services, the export of goods (fuel) is treated as a service under the ISIC code; the same reporting thresholds apply. No mandatory conversion ratio exists; the exporter may choose to convert to EUR or hold foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account for daily transactions) and Capital Escrow Account (for inbound investment funds)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Spain recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the E-Money Directive. Licensed EMIs (e.g., Bnext, N26, Revolut) can provide multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment services. However, for bunkering operations involving large-value trade settlements and standby letters of credit, traditional banks are preferred due to their ability to issue and confirm LCs. EMIs may face restrictions on providing credit or issuing guarantees. Legal constraints: EMIs must be authorized by the Banco de España or passported from another EU state; they are subject to AML/KYC obligations but may not offer full treasury services. For high-risk sectors like marine fuel supply, EMIs may impose enhanced due diligence or decline onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. Directors and beneficial owners must appear in person at a branch or at a notary to verify identity. Remote opening is possible for certain banks using video identification (e.g., via a notary or using the bank's digital onboarding tool), but for high-risk sectors like bunkering, banks typically mandate a physical interview with the compliance officer. The SL's legal representative (administrator) must provide original identification documents, proof of address, and corporate documents. For non-resident directors, a physical visit to Spain or a Spanish consulate may be required for notarization of powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification (ISIC 5222 – Marine bunkering) due to potential for sanctions evasion, smuggling, or money laundering via fuel trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Valid bunkering license issued by the Spanish Port Authority (Puertos del Estado) or regional port authority; (2) Detailed business plan and client list with due diligence on counterparties; (3) Evidence of compliance with international sanctions (e.g., OFAC, EU sanctions) through screening software; (4) Financial statements and proof of source of funds for initial capital; (5) Contracts with suppliers and buyers, including Incoterms and payment terms; (6) Tax registration certificates (CIF/NIF) and corporate registry extract; (7) Beneficial ownership declaration (UBO) with supporting documentation; (8) Any existing bank references or letters of credit from reputable institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with complex corporate chain (e.g., offshore entities) triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Full corporate structure chart with ownership percentages; (2) Legal opinion from a recognized law firm confirming the legitimacy of the structure; (3) Copies of passports and proof of address for all UBOs; (4) Business rationale for the structure (e.g., tax efficiency, operational presence); (5) Evidence of substance in Spain (e.g., office lease, local staff, bank account activity); (6) Regulatory filings (e.g., annual accounts) for all entities in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volumes or unusual payment patterns (e.g., rapid in/out flows) typical of bunkering operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Detailed cash flow projections and historical transaction records; (2) Contracts and invoices for each transaction; (3) Bill of lading and delivery receipts for fuel; (4) Explanation of the commercial cycle (e.g., purchase from refinery, sale to ship); (5) Compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) internal controls, including transaction monitoring procedures; (6) Appointment of a compliance officer and AML training certificates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound capital injections (e.g., equity contributions from non-resident shareholders) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with proper purpose codes. For equity injection, use purpose code 'P01' (Foreign Direct Investment) or 'P02' (Capital increase) as per Banco de España's statistical classification. The transfer must be accompanied by a notarized board resolution and updated corporate registry filing. Verification: The bank will require the underlying documentation (e.g., share subscription agreement, capital increase deed) and may report to the Banco de España. For loans from shareholders, use purpose code 'P03' (Financial loans) and ensure compliance with thin capitalization rules (30% EBITDA limit). The funds must be received in EUR or convertible currency; if in foreign currency, the bank will convert at market rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For bunkering operations, outbound payments to fuel suppliers and port authorities are typically executed via SWIFT MT103 (wire transfer) for direct payments, or via Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for larger, deferred payments. Standby LCs are used as guarantees for performance or payment. The bank will require underlying contracts and invoices. For payments to non-EU suppliers, ensure compliance with EU sanctions and export controls. For intra-EU payments, SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) transfers are efficient, but for non-EUR currencies, SWIFT is necessary. The bank may offer trade finance products such as documentary collections (D/P, D/A) and supply chain finance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards: Standard OTC forward contracts with maturities up to 12 months, available from major Spanish banks. No exchange control restrictions; contracts must be documented under ISDA or local master agreements.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): Permissible for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., certain Latin American currencies) but rarely used for EUR/USD or EUR/GBP. For bunkering, if trading with non-EUR currencies, NDFs may be used for hedging exposure to exotic currencies.

Currency Swaps: Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) are permissible for long-term hedging of principal and interest payments. Banks require a credit line and collateral. For bunkering, short-term FX swaps (swap de divisas) are common to manage liquidity in different currencies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Cuentas Anuales) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from approval by the General Meeting; must be filed within seven months after the financial year end (statutory annual deadline: by 31 July if financial year aligns with calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company cannot file or register subsequent documents; risk of closed registry file (cierre registral); financial penalties under Spanish Companies Act and potential strike-off after prolonged non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months and twenty-five days after the end of the tax year; for calendar-year companies, filed by 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges (recargo) from 5% to 20% depending on delay; late-payment interest; penalties from 50% to 150% of the tax shortfall; possible collection enforcement and criminal liability for fraudulent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Resident Companies (Modelo 200 includes corporate identity details; Modelo 100 for shareholders' resident individuals executed annually where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, aligned with Modelo 200 filing date (by 25 July after year-end); ancillary filing for certain shareholder-level information due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty regime under General Tax Law, including fixed penalties for failure to submit accurate information and possible professional misconduct liability for directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be deposited within one month after approval of annual accounts, and always within the seven-month period following the year-end (deadline: 31 July for calendar-year accounts); required for all SL entities irrespective of audit status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit leads to registry closure preventing filings; penalty regime under Spanish Mercantile Registry Regulations, including 1,200 EUR to 6,000 EUR penalties for repeated non-deposit; eventual strike-off risk after sustained non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Filing (annual confirmation of significant shareholding and beneficial ownership registry information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (under the UBO Internal Registry provisions; information supplied to the Single Digital Window for companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one month after the General Meeting approving the annual accounts; for calendar-year companies, generally by 30 June of the following year; updates required immediately upon any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Spanish anti-money-laundering law (Ley 10/2010), up to EUR 60,000 per material breach; registry closure for failure to maintain accurate UBO records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License / Operating Permit Renewal (port facility authorization for bunkering activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Comunidad Autónoma Port Authority / Spanish Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility (Puertos del Estado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal deadline typically set by the individual port authority authorization agreement; commonly due no later than 31 January for calendar-year port concessions or licenses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of bunkering operations; administrative fines; revocation of port operating license; prohibition from servicing vessels within Spanish territorial waters

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Hazardous Substances / Environmental Compliance Filing (marine fuel handling and transfer operations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico / Autonomous Community Environmental Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual environmental compliance report due by 31 March for the preceding calendar year, or per the terms of the environmental permit (integrated environmental authorization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from EUR 10,000 to EUR 600,000 under environmental liability rules; potential suspension of environmental authorization; criminal liability for negligent pollution incidents

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for Spanish SL entities if for two consecutive years at least two of the following thresholds are met: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit also required where the company is a dominant or dependent group member or if the General Meeting so resolves with at least 5% shareholding request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Normas de Contabilidad del PGC) as implemented in the Plan General Contable; IFRS mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed groups, but optional for non-listed groups within EU reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholders and beneficial owners must confirm their shareholding structure and UBO details annually. Changes in shareholding are registrable at the Mercantile Registry, and the company must maintain an internal registry (Libro Registro de Socios) reflecting any transfer within one month. The annual accounts filing must be accompanied by a statement confirming the UBO register is up to date; failure to update constitutes a reportable infringement under Spanish AML law. Share transfers not reflected in the books confer no membership rights vis-à-vis the company and remain unenforceable against third parties until registered.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Órgano de Administración)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 600 to EUR 2,200 (approx. USD 650 to USD 2,400) per annum, depending on service scope in Madrid or Barcelona
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,500 to EUR 8,500 (approx. USD 3,800 to USD 9,300) per audit engagement, depending on entity complexity and bunkering revenue volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly created entities and entities qualifying as startups may generally apply a 15% rate for the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain has no general tax holiday for an SL. Potential incentives include the 15% newly-created-entity rate, research and development credits, technological innovation credits, investment deductions where available, participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, capitalization deductions, and regional incentives subject to the applicable autonomous-community rules. The tonnage tax regime is potentially relevant to qualifying shipping activities but does not automatically apply to a marine-fuel-bunkering company. Petroleum products, excise duties, VAT, environmental taxes, port charges, and fuel-storage rules must be separately reviewed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Spanish tax losses generally do not expire after five years. Their utilization is subject to percentage limitations based principally on the taxpayer's net turnover and to an annual minimum offset threshold of EUR 1 million. The general limits are 70% of the pre-offset taxable base for taxpayers with turnover below EUR 20 million, 50% for turnover from EUR 20 million to below EUR 60 million, and 25% for turnover of EUR 60 million or more, with statutory special rules for tax groups, reorganizations, and certain transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic office using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative. Modelo 202 is used for applicable quarterly Corporate Income Tax prepayments. Modelo 232 is an annual related-party transaction and tax-haven information return where its thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: annual. Modelo 202: normally quarterly prepayments in April, October, and December. Modelo 232: annual where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is generally due within the 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July, with the payment-direct-debit deadline generally earlier. Modelo 202 is generally due from 1 to 20 April, October, and December. Modelo 232 is generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the tax period ends; for a 31 December year-end, this is normally November. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing and payment rules extend the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's Spanish tax identification number, legal name, registered address, tax period dates, accounting period, legal form, activity classification, and whether the return is an initial, supplementary, substitute, or rectifying filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-Spanish parent is not entered as the taxpayer merely because it owns the SL. The Spanish SL files using its own Spanish tax identification number. The foreign parent is disclosed only where required for ownership, related-party, beneficial-owner, group, or transaction reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the profit or loss before tax derived from the Spanish statutory accounts, generally based on the approved accounting records prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SL's Spanish accounting result. Do not substitute the foreign parent's consolidated result or a foreign branch computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record permanent and temporary increases or decreases for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, tax credits, limits on financial expenses, capitalization deductions, participation exemptions, and other Corporate Income Tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party payments to a foreign parent or affiliate must satisfy arm's-length, deductibility, withholding, beneficial-ownership, and substance requirements. Payments that are not incurred for the SL's business purpose or are unsupported may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report relevant related-party transactions and the applied transfer-pricing method where the form requires it. Separately file Modelo 232 when the statutory transaction, aggregate, or tax-haven thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border purchases of fuel or lubricants, management services, financing, guarantees, insurance, IP, agency services, and intercompany receivables or payables where the counterparty is related. Retain Spanish local-file and, where applicable, master-file documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter available tax-loss carryforwards, the amount utilized in the current period, and the remaining balance, applying the statutory utilization limits and the EUR 1 million minimum threshold rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses belong to the Spanish SL and cannot be transferred to the foreign shareholder outside a legally qualifying Spanish tax group or reorganization regime. Changes in ownership of loss-making companies may trigger anti-abuse restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, then apply the applicable rate, including any qualifying reduced rate or special regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard rate is 25%. Apply the 15% newly-created-entity rate only after confirming statutory qualification, commencement of economic activity, ownership restrictions, and the absence of an excluded restructuring or related-party succession.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying research and development, technological innovation, foreign-tax, employment, investment, and other statutory credits supported by contemporaneous records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes may be creditable only within statutory limits and subject to proof of payment and income attribution. A treaty relief position does not automatically create a Spanish tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset Modelo 202 prepayments, Spanish withholding suffered, and other legally creditable amounts against the final Corporate Income Tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not credit foreign withholding against Spanish Corporate Income Tax unless the amount qualifies under Spanish domestic law and the relevant treaty or statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the net amount payable, refundable, or zero after credits and prepayments. Select the permitted electronic payment, direct debit, or refund procedure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the bank account and payment mandate are compatible with AEAT requirements. A non-resident parent cannot replace the SL's filing or payment obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with tax due may trigger the voluntary late-filing surcharge under General Tax Law Article 27: generally 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first twelve months, and 15% after twelve months, plus applicable late-payment interest after twelve months. The surcharge is generally reduced by 25% if statutory payment conditions are met. Filing without economic damage may result in a fixed penalty generally of EUR 200, commonly reduced by 50% for electronic voluntary compliance where the statutory conditions apply. Failure to file or inaccurate filing after assessment may trigger penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to interest. Modelo 232 and transfer-pricing documentation failures may attract separate fixed or percentage-based penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply through Spanish implementation where the parent is a qualifying EU or qualifying EEA company, the minimum participation and holding-period conditions are satisfied, the anti-abuse requirements are met, and the recipient is subject to a qualifying tax. A 5% participation threshold and a minimum one-year holding requirement generally apply, with statutory alternatives for completing the holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify the applicable bilateral tax treaty, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provisions, minimum participation, holding period, and principal-purpose requirements, and retain ownership and substance evidence. Apply the reduced rate or exemption at source only where Spanish procedural requirements are satisfied. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. The Spanish SL remains responsible for withholding, filing Modelo 123, and reporting through Modelo 193 for dividends and similar income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish non-resident withholding is generally 24% on royalties and other qualifying income paid to non-residents, reduced generally to 19% for residents of the EU or qualifying EEA jurisdictions, subject to statutory conditions. Interest is generally subject to 19% domestic withholding. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated EU companies meeting participation, holding-period, beneficial-owner, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements. Tax treaties frequently reduce dividends to treaty-specific rates, interest to 0% or a reduced rate, and royalties to a reduced rate, often 5%, 8%, 10%, or 12%, but the exact rate depends on the recipient's country and the relevant treaty. Spain also has exemptions for certain qualifying financial-market and listed-security income. Spanish withholding forms and certificates must be retained.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain does not use one universal monetary threshold for all mandatory local-file and master-file obligations. Full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies to material related-party transactions, subject to statutory simplified-documentation rules. Documentation is generally not required for transactions with the same related party that do not exceed EUR 250,000 in aggregate for the tax period under the same valuation method, subject to exclusions. A master file is generally relevant for Spanish entities belonging to a group required to prepare consolidated accounts, particularly where consolidated group turnover reaches EUR 750 million for Country-by-Country Reporting purposes. Modelo 232 is generally triggered by transaction-category thresholds, including transactions of the same type and method exceeding EUR 250,000, specific transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 in certain tax-haven categories, or related-party transactions exceeding 50% of the entity's turnover, subject to the current form instructions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the statutory methods cannot reliably be applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the beneficial-ownership and EU exemption rules, the General Anti-Abuse Rule, the anti-tax-avoidance rule, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, treaty principal-purpose tests, and deductibility requirements. A Spanish bunkering SL should maintain real operational capacity proportionate to its business, including personnel or outsourced operational control, port and fuel-supply contracts, inventory and delivery records, risk control, banking activity, accounting records, decision-making evidence, and commercial rationale. A conduit entity receiving dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees without functions, assets, risks, or decision-making authority faces denial of relief, income recharacterization, withholding assessments, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing bunker sales, under-recording fuel volumes, fabricating supplier invoices, diverting customer receipts, creating undeclared cash settlements, or claiming fictitious expenses or losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with repayment of tax and interest. Tax fraud becomes a criminal offense where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period and tax, interest, and criminal fines apply. Ordinary tax fraud may carry imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases may carry two to six years' imprisonment and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability to the company, tax liability as collaborating or subsidiarily liable persons, disqualification consequences, asset seizure, and criminal liability. Imprisonment is possible in qualifying criminal cases. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court where necessary to secure criminal proceedings; there is no automatic travel ban for ordinary tax arrears.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using false intra-EU acquisitions, carousel structures, incorrect VAT zero-rating, diversion of duty-suspended fuel, falsified excise movement records, or selling marked or duty-exempt fuel for unauthorized marine use.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid VAT and excise duties, late-payment interest, administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture of fuel and equipment, suspension or loss of excise authorizations, and potential criminal prosecution where statutory thresholds or organized-fraud conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or knowingly facilitate fraudulent VAT or excise arrangements may face joint or subsidiary tax liability, civil restitution, administrative disqualification, asset seizure, and imprisonment in criminal cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing imported fuel or services from a related foreign entity, underpricing exports, using unsupported management fees, shifting bunker margins to a low-tax affiliate, or maintaining debt and guarantees inconsistent with the SL's functions and credit capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustments, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Documentation-related penalties may be fixed or calculated by reference to the undeclared or incorrectly valued amounts under the Corporate Income Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where the conduct is intentional, negligent, or part of a tax-fraud scheme. Criminal exposure arises if the resulting tax fraud exceeds the criminal threshold or forms part of falsification, money laundering, or organized fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees through the SL or a foreign holding company that lacks commercial substance, retaining no real control over the income, or claiming treaty or EU exemptions solely to obtain a tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemption, withholding at the full domestic rate, payment of arrears and interest, General Anti-Abuse Rule assessments, and penalties for incorrect withholding or reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur withholding-agent liability and civil restitution obligations. Intentional participation in sham arrangements may create criminal tax-fraud or document-fraud exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained payments from opaque shipowners, sanctioned parties, shell trading companies, high-risk jurisdictions, or unrelated third parties; failing to identify beneficial owners; structuring payments; or ignoring suspicious bunker-fuel transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in public or private reprimands, fines that can reach the higher of statutory fixed amounts or a percentage of the transaction or annual turnover, temporary management or activity prohibitions, and loss of authorization. Criminal money laundering may carry imprisonment generally from six months to six years and fines from one to three times the value of the assets, with aggravated consequences in specified cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, compliance officers, and directors may be personally fined, disqualified, and prosecuted where they knowingly participate in or negligently permit laundering. Asset freezing, confiscation, civil restitution, and court-ordered travel restrictions may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions, export controls, and restricted-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying fuel, lubricants, financing, or port services to sanctioned vessels, owners, charterers, or jurisdictions; disguising the vessel's identity or destination; or processing payments through prohibited counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EU and Spanish sanctions may impose asset freezes, prohibitions on making funds or economic resources available, administrative fines, authorization loss, contract invalidity, and criminal liability under applicable implementing legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel who authorize or knowingly facilitate prohibited transactions may face personal administrative and criminal liability, confiscation, civil damages, and court-ordered restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed bunkering, port, environmental, or fuel-quality operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying marine fuel without required port, maritime, storage, excise, environmental, safety, or fuel-quality authorizations; operating unauthorized barges or tanks; or delivering fuel that fails applicable sulfur, traceability, or technical standards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include administrative fines, suspension or revocation of licenses, detention of vessels, seizure of fuel, cleanup and remediation costs, environmental liability, civil claims, and criminal prosecution for serious pollution or safety offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil environmental liability, administrative liability, and criminal prosecution where they ordered, knowingly tolerated, or negligently failed to prevent the unlawful operation. Courts may impose restitution, confiscation, and restrictions on management activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to retain records and file statutory information
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain invoices, delivery notes, meter readings, bills of lading, customs and excise records, related-party agreements, local-file support, beneficial-owner files, or electronic accounting records; or failure to file Modelo 200, 202, 232, 123, or 193.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed or percentage-based penalties may apply for failure to file, incomplete or inaccurate information, obstruction, deficient accounting, withholding failures, and transfer-pricing documentation failures. Assessments may include tax, interest, and denial of deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SL's directors may be secondarily liable for tax debts where statutory conditions for administrator liability are met, especially after repeated non-compliance or dissolution without satisfying creditors. Civil claims, disqualification, and criminal exposure may follow where concealment or falsification is involved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Asset stripping and improper profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends while the SL is insolvent or without distributable profits, making undocumented shareholder loans, transferring fuel inventory or cash below market value, or extracting funds that prejudice tax or trade creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, creditor claims, insolvency clawback, director liability, tax adjustments, withholding assessments, and possible insolvency or fraud offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may owe civil restitution, creditor compensation, and insolvency-related damages; may be disqualified from management; and may face criminal liability for fraudulent insolvency, misappropriation, or creditor prejudice. Travel restrictions are court-dependent and not automatic.
